guide.h: How to make an invoice in five minutes
p: An invoice tells your client what you did, what it costs and how to pay you. Getting it right first time means fewer follow-up emails and money in your account sooner. Here’s the quickest route with BillFlow.
list: Add your business name, address and logo, plus a tax ID such as a VAT number, ABN or EIN if you have one.
Add your client’s legal name, address and, for a business client, their tax ID.
Set the invoice number, invoice date and a due date.
List each service or product on its own line with quantity and rate.
Choose your tax, add a discount if you agreed one, and check the totals and amount in words.
Add your payment details, pick a style and download the PDF.

guide.h: What every invoice should include
p: Rules vary from country to country, but almost everywhere a professional invoice shows a clear title, your name or trading name and contact details, the client’s name and address, a unique invoice number, the date of issue, a description of what you supplied, the amounts and the total. A due date isn’t always required by law, but it’s the single most useful line for getting paid on time.

Describe the work in words the client will recognise, such as “Homepage redesign, 2 revision rounds” rather than just “Design”. Showing quantity and rate makes the maths easy to check, which keeps the invoice moving through approval.

guide.h: Tax on your invoice: VAT, GST or sales tax
p: Whether you add tax depends on where you are and whether you’re registered. In the UK only VAT-registered businesses may charge VAT, and the standard rate is 20%. In Australia, GST of 10% applies once you’re registered, and registered suppliers issue a “Tax invoice”. In the EU, rates differ by country and cross-border business services often fall under the reverse charge. The US has no national VAT; sales tax is set by each state and many services aren’t taxed. In India, registered businesses charge GST split into CGST and SGST or IGST.
BillFlow suggests the usual tax for your location, but you can change it or remove it. If you aren’t sure what applies to you, check with an accountant or your local tax authority.

guide.h: Common invoicing mistakes to avoid
p: Small errors are the usual reason an accounts team sends an invoice back. Run through this list before you download.
list: Reusing an invoice number or skipping numbers without a reason.
Leaving out the due date, which gives the client no deadline.
Getting the client’s legal name or tax ID wrong.
Charging VAT or GST when you aren’t registered, or forgetting it when you are.
Forgetting payment details, so the client has to ask how to pay.
Sending an editable file instead of a PDF.

guide.h: How to write a freelance invoice
p: A freelance invoice is a request for payment, but it’s also your record of what was agreed and delivered. Clients with a finance team often won’t release money without a proper invoice, so it pays to get the basics right from your very first project.
list: Add your name or trading name, address and email, plus your logo if you have one.
Enter the client’s name and billing address exactly as they want it in their books.
Give the invoice a unique number and set the invoice date and a due date.
List the work as a milestone, a fixed-fee deliverable, or hours multiplied by your rate.
Set tax to none unless you’re registered for VAT, GST or sales tax.
Add how you’d like to be paid, then download the PDF and send it.

guide.h: Line items clients approve quickly
p: Specific descriptions save you a round of questions. Instead of “Design work”, write “Landing page design, milestone 1 of 3” or “Copy edits, 4 hours”. When you bill by the hour, the quantity and rate columns show exactly how you reached the total.

If a client asks for a change after you’ve sent the invoice, issue a corrected one with a new number rather than quietly editing the old PDF. Use the notes for your payment terms, a thank-you, or a line about what the next milestone covers.

guide.h: Tax and registration for freelancers
p: Most countries only expect you to add VAT, GST or sales tax once you’re registered, and each sets its own threshold. In the UK it’s currently £90,000 of taxable turnover; in Australia, A$75,000; in India, ₹20 lakh for most service providers. In the US there’s no national VAT and many freelance services aren’t subject to state sales tax, though rules vary by state. Once you register, add your tax ID and turn tax on. When in doubt, ask a local accountant.

guide.h: Getting paid faster as a freelancer
p: Make paying you the easiest task on your client’s list. Add a payment link from PayPal, Stripe or Wise and BillFlow prints a scan-to-pay QR code on the invoice. For larger amounts, add bank details with the codes your client’s bank needs: IBAN and SWIFT/BIC internationally, a routing number in the US, a sort code in the UK or a BSB in Australia.

On bigger projects, ask for an advance and bill the rest by milestone so you’re never carrying a month of unpaid work. Send each invoice the day the milestone is approved, while the work is fresh in your client’s mind.

guide.h: How to structure a consulting invoice
p: Consulting is usually billed by the hour, by the day, as a fixed project fee or as a monthly retainer. Your invoice should mirror your engagement letter, using the same rates and wording, so the client’s finance team can match the two documents and approve payment without coming back to you.
list: Hourly: one line per type of work, with hours as quantity and your hourly rate as rate.
Day rate: workshops, on-site days or board sessions, with days as quantity.
Retainer: one line such as “Advisory retainer, October 2026” at the monthly fee.
Fixed fee: one line per phase, such as diagnostic, recommendations and implementation support.

guide.h: Hourly vs fixed fee vs retainer
p: Hourly billing is fair when the scope is uncertain, but clients often ask what the hours went on, so keep brief notes and summarise them in the line description. Fixed fees reward efficient work and are easier for clients to budget, but they need a tightly written scope. Retainers give you steady income in return for guaranteed availability; say in the notes what the retainer covers and how extra hours are charged.

guide.h: Tax on consulting fees
p: If you’re registered for VAT or GST, add your tax ID and your client’s and turn on the right tax. A UK VAT-registered consultant typically charges 20% VAT, an Australian one 10% GST on a tax invoice, and an Indian one GST as CGST and SGST or IGST, with a SAC code such as 998311 for management consulting. Advising a business in another EU country often falls under the reverse charge. In the US, consulting is frequently outside state sales tax, but confirm your state’s rules.
Tax can be set per line, so an invoice that mixes fees with other items still adds up correctly. For anything unusual, a quick check with your accountant is worth it.

guide.h: Getting consulting invoices approved and paid
p: Set clear payment terms, such as 30 days from the invoice date, and enter the actual due date so there’s no room for doubt.
list: Quote the purchase order or contract reference in the notes if the client uses one.
Address the invoice to the legal entity named in the contract, not just the person who hired you.
Bill retainers at the start of the month and hourly work at the end, on the same date each time.
For international clients, give an IBAN and SWIFT/BIC or a payment link so fees and delays stay low.

guide.h: How to invoice a website project
p: Website projects run for weeks and often change shape halfway through, so a single bill at the end is risky. Most developers agree an advance and then invoice in milestones tied to something the client can see and sign off.
list: Advance on signing, for example 30 to 50% of the quote.
Design approval: wireframes and page designs signed off.
Development complete: site built on a staging link for review.
Launch and handover: site live, logins and files handed over.

guide.h: Hosting, domains and third-party costs
p: Clients often ask you to buy the domain, hosting, premium themes, plugins or paid APIs for them. Bill these on separate lines from your own work and state the period they cover, such as “Domain renewal, 1 year” or “Hosting, Nov 2026 to Oct 2027”. The client can then tell recurring running costs apart from one-off fees for your time.

Where you can, register domains and hosting in the client’s name so they own them outright. If you pay and recharge the cost, the tax treatment of these pass-through expenses differs between countries, so ask your accountant how to show them.

guide.h: Tax for web developers in different countries
p: If you aren’t registered for any indirect tax, keep tax set to none and invoice your fees. Once you are, turn on the tax that applies: VAT in the UK and EU, GST in Australia or India, or state sales tax where your US state taxes the service. Add your tax ID and your client’s; for an EU business client in another member state, the reverse charge may apply. Indian developers can also add a SAC code per line and get the CGST and SGST or IGST split suggested from both GSTINs.

Working for an overseas client adds one more question: whether the sale counts as an export of services. Rules differ, and in some places, such as India under a LUT, exported services can be zero-rated. Confirm how your own country treats it before you send the first invoice.

guide.h: Mistakes web developers should avoid
p: Use the notes to record what has already been paid, as this template does with “50% advance received”, so your final invoice and the client’s records always agree.
list: Handing over admin access or final code before the last invoice is paid.
Absorbing change requests instead of billing them as their own line.
Burying annual maintenance inside the build fee rather than invoicing it each period.
Quoting in one currency and invoicing in another without agreeing it first.
Leaving the advance out of the notes, so the client is unsure what balance remains.

guide.h: How to write a graphic design invoice
p: A design invoice works best when it reads like a summary of the brief. Give each deliverable its own line with enough detail that the client recognises it at once: “Logo design, 3 concepts, 2 revision rounds” says far more than “Logo”.
list: Upload your own logo so the invoice feels like part of your brand.
Pick one of BillFlow’s 11 visual styles to suit your work.
Itemise deliverables, using quantity for repeat work such as social posts or banners.
Add a separate line for revision rounds beyond what you agreed.

guide.h: Revisions, usage rights and final files
p: Revision rounds are where design projects quietly lose money. Agree the number of included rounds in your quote, say two, then bill further rounds on their own line, per round or per hour. Mention the included rounds in the line description so an extra charge never feels unexpected.

Be clear about usage rights too. A logo for a company’s permanent identity is a different job from a one-off event poster, and you may price full ownership differently from limited use. Write what the client receives in the notes, for example “Rights to the final logo transfer on full payment; working files and unused concepts remain with the designer”.

guide.h: Tax for independent designers
p: Many independent designers start out below their country’s registration threshold, which is why this template has tax switched off. Once you register, add your tax ID and turn on the right tax: VAT in the UK (20% standard rate) or the EU, GST in Australia (10%) or India, or US sales tax only if your state taxes design services. Indian designers can add a SAC code per line, often 998391 for specialty design, but confirm the right code with an accountant. If you’re unsure, a short conversation with a local adviser is cheaper than correcting invoices later.

guide.h: Getting paid before you hand over files
p: Share watermarked or low-resolution previews for approval, then release the final high-resolution and source files once the invoice is settled. Say so plainly in the notes, as this template does, so it reads as your standard policy rather than a negotiation. For larger branding projects, invoice an advance before you start on concepts.

Then make payment effortless. A PayPal, Stripe or Wise link printed with a scan-to-pay QR suits small businesses and quick jobs, while agencies and larger companies usually prefer a bank transfer, so add the account details and codes they need.

guide.h: Deposits, balances and getting paid
p: Most photographers take a non-refundable deposit to hold the date and collect the balance on the day or before handing over the final gallery or album. Put your policy in the notes, along with the date the deposit arrived and when the remainder is due.

faq.q: What is a proforma invoice?
faq.a: A proforma invoice is a preliminary bill sent before a sale is completed. It sets out the goods or services, quantities and expected price, but it is not a final invoice or a tax invoice and isn’t recorded as a sale.

faq.q: Is a proforma invoice legally binding?
faq.a: Generally no. It is a formal quote that confirms the terms you are offering. Once the order is confirmed and delivered, you issue a regular invoice for the actual supply.

faq.q: Should a proforma invoice show VAT, GST or sales tax?
faq.a: Showing the tax that will apply helps the buyer see the full cost. It doesn’t create a tax liability by itself, and the buyer can’t reclaim tax using it; that needs the final invoice.

faq.q: Does a proforma invoice need a number?

faq.q: How long is a proforma invoice valid?
faq.a: There is no standard period. You set it, commonly 7 to 30 days, and state it in the notes so the buyer knows when prices may change.

faq.a: Only GST-registered businesses issue tax invoices, which let the buyer claim a GST credit. If you’re not registered for GST, you issue an ordinary invoice: no GST and no “Tax invoice” heading, but you should still quote your ABN.

faq.q: When do I have to register for GST?
faq.a: You must register once your GST turnover reaches A$75,000 a year (A$150,000 for non-profit organisations), and you can register voluntarily below that. Check the ATO website or ask your accountant if you’re close to the threshold.

faq.q: What must an Australian tax invoice show?
faq.a: The words “Tax invoice”, your identity and ABN, the date of issue, a description of what you sold including quantity and price, and the GST amount, or a clear statement that the total includes GST.

faq.q: Do I need the buyer’s details on a tax invoice?
faq.a: For tax invoices of A$1,000 or more, yes: show the buyer’s identity or ABN. BillFlow has a tax ID field for your client, so you can add their ABN alongside their name and address.

faq.q: What happens if I don’t quote my ABN?
faq.a: If you invoice another business without quoting an ABN, they may have to withhold tax from your payment at the top rate. Adding your ABN in your tax ID field avoids that.

faq.q: How do I switch this to an invoice without GST?
faq.a: Change the tax setting to none and change the document title from “Tax Invoice” to “Invoice”. Keep your ABN in the tax ID field so it still prints on the invoice.

guide.h: Tax invoice or plain invoice?
p: In Australia the word “tax” on your invoice matters. A tax invoice is issued by a business registered for GST, and it’s the document your customer needs to claim a GST credit. You must register for GST once your annual GST turnover reaches A$75,000 (A$150,000 for non-profits), and you can choose to register earlier.

If you’re not registered, you can’t charge GST and you shouldn’t call your document a tax invoice. Issue an ordinary invoice instead, and still quote your ABN. In BillFlow that means setting the tax to none and changing the title to “Invoice”. If you register for GST part-way through the year, switch to tax invoices from your registration date and keep your invoice numbers running in the same sequence.

guide.h: What a tax invoice must include
p: For sales under A$1,000, a tax invoice must show:
list: The words “Tax invoice”, clearly at the top
Your identity (business or trading name) and your ABN
The date the invoice was issued
A brief description of each item, with quantity and price
The GST amount, or a statement that the total includes GST
Which items are taxable, if some are GST-free

guide.h: Invoices of A$1,000 or more
p: When the total is A$1,000 or more, the tax invoice must also show the buyer’s identity or ABN. Add your client’s business name in the client details and their ABN in the client tax ID field, and BillFlow prints both on the PDF.

This template is set up for a GST-registered business: the title reads “Tax Invoice”, the tax is labelled GST and each line is at 10%. If an item is GST-free, set that line to 0% and describe it clearly so your customer knows no GST was charged on it.

guide.h: Your ABN and getting paid
p: Always put your ABN on invoices to other businesses, whether or not you’re registered for GST. If you don’t quote one, the business paying you may have to withhold tax from your payment at the top rate, which is a hassle nobody wants.

Australian clients usually pay by bank transfer, so add your account name, BSB and account number. You can also paste a payment link, such as PayPal or Stripe, and BillFlow adds a scan-to-pay QR code. Set a due date and a short note like “Payment within 14 days” to keep things moving. If you’re unsure how GST applies to what you sell, the ATO website or your accountant can confirm.

faq.q: What must a GST invoice contain?
faq.a: Supplier name, address and GSTIN; a unique invoice number and date; recipient details (and GSTIN if registered); HSN/SAC codes; taxable value; GST rate and amount (CGST+SGST or IGST); place of supply and the total.

faq.q: When do I charge CGST + SGST instead of IGST?
faq.a: Charge CGST + SGST when you and your client are in the same state (intra-state supply). Charge IGST when the supply is to another state (inter-state). BillFlow suggests the right option from the first two digits of both GSTINs.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to write “Tax Invoice” on a GST invoice?
faq.a: Yes. A tax invoice issued by a GST-registered supplier should be clearly titled “Tax Invoice”. This template uses that title by default.

faq.q: How many digits of HSN or SAC code do I need?
faq.a: For B2B invoices, businesses with aggregate turnover up to ₹5 crore must show at least a 4-digit HSN/SAC code, and those above ₹5 crore must show 6 digits. Check with your CA for B2C rules that apply to you.

faq.q: How can I check if a GSTIN is valid?
faq.a: A GSTIN has 15 characters and starts with a two-digit state code. BillFlow checks the format as you type. To confirm the number is active and belongs to your client, search it on the official GST portal.

faq.q: Can my client claim input tax credit on this invoice?
faq.a: Input tax credit depends on a valid tax invoice with correct GSTINs and on the invoice being reported in your GST returns. Make sure the details are accurate and file your returns on time.

guide.h: GST invoice format: the required fields
p: Rule 46 of the CGST Rules lists what a GST tax invoice must contain. If any of these are missing, your client may struggle to claim input tax credit and you may be asked to reissue the bill. The core fields are:
list: Supplier’s name, address and GSTIN
A unique, consecutive invoice number for the financial year, and the date of issue
Recipient’s name and address, and GSTIN if they are registered
Description of goods or services with the HSN or SAC code
Quantity, unit and taxable value after any discount
GST rate and tax amount, shown as CGST and SGST or as IGST
Place of supply for inter-state supplies
Signature or digital signature of the supplier or an authorised person

guide.h: CGST + SGST or IGST: which one applies
p: The split depends on where the supply happens. When you and the buyer are in the same state, the supply is intra-state and the GST is divided equally: an 18% rate becomes 9% CGST plus 9% SGST. When the supply crosses a state border, the full 18% is charged as IGST.

The first two digits of a GSTIN are the state code, for example 27 for Maharashtra and 29 for Karnataka. BillFlow compares the codes in your GSTIN and your client’s GSTIN and suggests intra-state or inter-state for you. BillFlow does not have a separate place of supply field, so if that needs to be printed, add it in the notes, for example “Place of supply: Karnataka (29)”.

guide.h: How to fill this GST invoice format
p: Start with your GSTIN and your client’s GSTIN; the format check flags a number that is the wrong length or shape. Then add each line with its HSN or SAC code and GST rate. Different lines can carry different rates, so a 5% item and an 18% service can sit on the same invoice.

Add a discount percentage if you offered one, and the taxable value and tax are worked out on the discounted amount. The total is printed in figures and in words using lakh and crore. Keep the declaration note, sign the printed copy or add your signature, and download the PDF for your records.

guide.h: Mistakes that cause GST invoice rejections
p: The most common problem is a wrong GSTIN, often a single swapped character. Next come the wrong tax type, such as charging IGST on a sale within the same state, and missing or mismatched HSN/SAC codes. Breaks in the invoice number series also attract questions during an audit. Finally, make sure the invoice values match what you report in your GST returns, because your client’s credit depends on it. If you are unsure about the rate for a particular item, confirm it with your CA before billing.

faq.q: Do I charge GST to foreign clients?
faq.a: Export of services is zero-rated. If you've filed a Letter of Undertaking (LUT), you invoice without IGST and add the LUT declaration shown in the notes.

faq.q: Which currencies are supported?
faq.a: INR, USD, EUR, GBP and AED. The amount in words follows the chosen currency.

faq.q: Can I invoice a foreign client in rupees?
faq.a: You can, but the invoice currency should match what your contract says, and overseas clients usually find it simpler to pay in their own currency. BillFlow lets you switch between INR, USD, EUR, GBP and AED, and the amount in words updates to match.

faq.q: What is a FIRA or FIRC and do I need one?
faq.a: It’s a Foreign Inward Remittance Advice or Certificate issued by your bank as proof that foreign money was received. Keep one for every export invoice, as it supports your claim that the supply was a zero-rated export.

faq.q: Do I need to file a new LUT every year?
faq.a: Yes. An LUT applies for one financial year, so file a fresh one on the GST portal before you invoice exports without IGST in the new year.

faq.q: Should I add a GSTIN for an overseas client?
faq.a: No. Foreign businesses don’t have an Indian GSTIN, so leave that field empty and enter their company name, address and country instead. Your own GSTIN still goes on the invoice if you’re registered.

guide.h: How to invoice a foreign client from India
list: Set the currency you agreed with the client: USD, EUR, GBP or AED. The amount in words follows that currency.
Enter the client’s company name and full overseas address, including country. Leave the client GSTIN empty.
Describe each service and add its SAC code, such as 998314 for software design and development.
If you’re GST-registered with a valid LUT, keep tax on “No tax” and add the LUT declaration in the notes, as this template does.
Add bank details for an international transfer, set a due date and download the PDF.

guide.h: GST on export of services and the LUT
p: Services you supply from India to a client outside India, paid for in foreign exchange, generally count as an export of services. Exports are zero-rated: you can either pay IGST and claim a refund, or file a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) on the GST portal and invoice without paying IGST at all. The LUT route is usually simpler, as none of your money is locked up waiting for a refund.

An LUT covers one financial year, so renew it before each new year begins. If you aren’t registered under GST because your turnover is below the threshold, you simply invoice without GST. Whether a particular contract qualifies as an export can depend on its details, so check with your CA if you’re unsure.

guide.h: Getting paid from abroad
p: Overseas clients usually pay by SWIFT bank transfer or through a payment platform. Put your account holder name, account number, bank, branch and IFSC on the invoice; type the IFSC into BillFlow and the bank and branch fill in automatically. A SWIFT transfer also needs your bank’s SWIFT code, so get it from your bank and add it in the notes.

When the money arrives, your bank can issue a FIRA or FIRC confirming the inward remittance. Keep it alongside a copy of the invoice. It’s your evidence that payment came in as foreign exchange, which matters for your GST records and returns.

guide.h: Mistakes to avoid on international invoices
list: Adding 18% GST to an overseas client out of habit, when an LUT lets you invoice without IGST.
Forgetting the LUT declaration in the notes.
Invoicing in INR when the contract is in dollars or euros, leaving the client to guess the exchange rate.
Leaving out the client’s full address and country.
Not chasing a missing FIRA or FIRC until it’s time to file returns.

templates.intro: If your business in India isn’t registered under GST, you can still issue a clean, professional invoice. Leave tax off and list your services and the amount due in rupees.

faq.q: Can I issue an invoice without a GST number?
faq.a: Yes. Businesses below the GST registration threshold can issue a normal invoice without GSTIN or tax. Just don't show any GST amount.

faq.q: What is a bill of supply?
faq.a: A bill of supply is issued by composition dealers or for exempt supplies, where no GST is charged. Change the document title to “Bill of Supply” if that applies to you.

faq.q: Do I need GST registration as a freelancer?
faq.a: Usually only once your aggregate turnover from services crosses ₹20 lakh in a financial year (₹10 lakh in special category states). Some activities need registration regardless of turnover, so confirm your case with a CA.

faq.q: Can I charge GST if I am not registered?
faq.a: No. Only GST-registered businesses can collect GST. If you are not registered, bill only your fee and do not add any tax line.

faq.q: Should I mention my PAN on an invoice without GST?
faq.a: It isn’t required on every invoice, but many business clients ask for it for their records and tax deductions. You can add it in the notes, for example “PAN: ABCDE1234F”.

faq.q: Can a composition dealer use this format?
faq.a: Composition-scheme taxpayers are registered but must issue a bill of supply, not a tax invoice. Change the document title to “Bill of Supply”, add your GSTIN and do not show any GST on the bill.

guide.h: Who can issue an invoice without GST
p: If you are not registered under GST, you cannot charge GST, but you still need a proper invoice to get paid and to keep your own accounts in order. This applies to many freelancers, tutors, designers, consultants and home businesses.

GST registration generally becomes compulsory once your aggregate turnover crosses ₹20 lakh a year for services (₹10 lakh in special category states) or ₹40 lakh for goods in most states. Below that, registration is optional. Some situations, such as certain inter-state sales of goods or selling through e-commerce platforms, can require registration earlier, so check with your CA if you are close to the limit or sell online.

guide.h: How to make an invoice without GST
p: For example, a ₹15,000 copywriting project is billed as exactly ₹15,000, with the amount in words reading “Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only”.
list: Choose “No tax” as the tax mode so no GST lines appear.
Leave the GSTIN fields blank.
Enter your name or business name, address, email and phone number.
Add your client’s details and a unique invoice number and date.
Describe each service clearly with the quantity and your rate.
Keep the note “Supplier not registered under GST” so the client’s accounts team knows why no tax is shown.
Add your UPI ID or bank details and download the PDF.

guide.h: Invoice without GST vs bill of supply
p: An invoice without GST is what an unregistered person issues. It carries no GSTIN because you don’t have one.

A bill of supply is a GST document issued by registered persons who cannot charge tax on a particular sale, such as composition-scheme taxpayers or businesses supplying exempt goods or services. It shows the supplier’s GSTIN but no GST amount. If that describes you, retitle the document “Bill of Supply” in BillFlow instead of “Invoice”.

guide.h: Mistakes to avoid when you are not registered
p: Never add GST to your bill just because a client asks for it or because larger vendors do. Collecting tax without registration is not allowed, and it creates trouble for both of you. Do not print a made-up or borrowed GSTIN either.

Keep an eye on your total turnover across all clients, not just one. Once you approach the threshold, plan your registration in advance so you can switch to tax invoices from the right date. Until then, keep every invoice in a numbered series so your income record is complete when you file your income tax return.
